editorial:
Imagine finishing school only to find out you own a hotel in a beautiful lakeside town. That is exactly what happens to Mutz, a young woman who thinks she has hit the jackpot. But when she arrives at the Jungfrau, she finds out it is actually a total wreck. To make things worse, there is a fancy rival hotel across the way called the Mönch. The funny part is that Mutz meets a charming guy named Konrad on the train, only to realize later that he owns the rival hotel. Their families have hated each other for years, which turns this into a hilarious battle of the hotels. It is a lighthearted story about young love and a stubborn family feud.

You will love how quickly the pace moves as Mutz works to fix up her run-down building to beat Konrad. The acting is sweet and the chemistry between the two leads makes the rivalry feel playful rather than mean. While the 1930s style might feel a bit old for some, the comedy still lands well.
endingExplained: After a lot of fighting and trying to outdo each other, Mutz and Konrad realize that their feelings for each other are stronger than their families' old grudge. The rivalry ends when they decide to stop competing and start working together. They eventually fall in love and bridge the gap between the two hotels. The movie wraps up with a happy ending where love wins over the long-standing family feud, leaving both hotels successful.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-school rom-coms and happy endings.
